newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel investigates U.S. East Jerusalem offices.
newsitem.headline: Israel investigates U.S. East Jerusalem offices.

text.p: The United States has asked Israel to explain why its police have twice investigated an American-run office in Arab East Jerusalem, a U.S. consulate spokesman said on Tuesday.

Israel has been investigating offices in Arab East Jerusalem it suspects might be run by the Palestinian Authority as part of its fight with the Palestinians over who will ultimately be sovereign in Arab East Jerusalem.

U.S. officials said Israeli security personnel came to the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs (NDI) on February 27 and March 10, despite being told the non-governmental organisation was American.
"This is an American institution. It's based in Washington ...Nobody understands why this is happening, so we've asked for clarification," consulate spokesman Duncan McGinnis said.
Sean Carroll, NDI head, told Reuters: "It sort of looks like some kind of bothering of non-governmental organisations in East Jerusalem."
NDI works with the Palestinian Legislative Council to strengthen democratic institutions. One of NDI's founding board members was Madeleine Albright, now U.S. secretary of state.
"She served as vice chair for a time," Carroll added.

A police spokeswoman said security forces were now satisfied that the NDI was not run by the Palestinian Authority. She said during the first visit a woman at the office had responded "yes" when asked if the NDI had anything to do with the Palestinian Authority.
She told Reuters on the second visit police met Carroll, who had not been at the office the first time, and he proved to them the office was under U.S. auspices.
Israeli police this month issued closure orders to four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem, saying they were run by the Palestinian Authority.
Israel says offices working under the Palestinian Authority, which runs self-rule areas in other parts of the West Bank and in the Gaza Strip, are barred from Jerusalem under interim peace deals.
Palestinians deny the offices are linked to the Palestinian Authority, insisting that the closure orders were part of an Israeli intimidation campaign.

"These are racist measures against any institution set up by Palestinians in Jerusalem because they want to disperse the Palestinian people from the city," Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo told Voice of Palestine radio.

The status of Jerusalem is up for negotiation at final peace talks slated to begin on March 17. Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it shortly after. Palestinians want it as capital of a future state.
The closure orders against the four Palestinian offices have yet to be executed, pending Palestinian appeals.
